title: Twentyeight I was. She twentythree. When we left Lombard street west something changed. Could never like it again after Rudy.
html_source: Bloom imparts that he and Molly have not had regular sex since Rudy died ten years ago. He says that he could never like it again. Or does he? He could be saying that Molly said that she “could never like it again after Rudy.” Or does he just think that Molly feels that way? We don’t know – but when we finally get Molly’s side of things, she doesn’t declare those feelings.
